KEY MESSAGE 1...High pressure builds in from southwest Quebec 
with some patchy fog and stratus this morning that will burn off
in the late morning. The mid and upper level flow will be west 
to northwest the next several days, as upstream ridging sets up 
over the Upper Midwest, Great Lakes Region and Ontario with a 
strong closed H500 anticyclone centered over the Lower MS and TN
Valleys. The cold front from this morning will slowly lift back
to north/northeast from PA/NJ and western NY with increasing 
clouds and showers building in from the west/southwest in the 
mid to late afternoon. We slowed down the PoPs/showers based on 
the latest short-range guidance and CAMS. Temps will be 
seasonable today with upper 60s to upper 70s across the region 
with moderate humidity levels with dewpoints in the upper 50s to
mid 70s. 

Tonight, the isentropic lift increases ahead of the warm front
and a short-wave rolls across the ridge into upstate NY. A wave
of low pressure or decaying MCS rides along the boundary 
bringing periods of showers and some thunderstorms due to 
elevated instability /Showalter stability indices below 0/ ahead
of the front and wave. Latest HREF guidance indicates mean 
MUCAPEs generally 500 J/kg or less with 0-6 km shear 35-40 KT. 
With the parcels elevated we are not expecting severe 
thunderstorms. Rainfall could become moderate to locally heavy 
with PWATs rising into the 1.5-2.0" range about 1 to 2 STDEVs 
above normal. The CAMs have shifted slightly further south with 
the coverage of the showers and thunderstorms with the most 
widespread coverage from the Mohawk Valley/Capital Region 
southward, but slight variations may occur. Ponding of water on 
roadways may occur in a few spots. Gridded FFG values remain 
high right now with drier weather recently. WPC maintains a 
Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 4) in their Day 1 ERO. An isolated 
flash flood threat can not be ruled out in case any training
occurs, but that looks low on the onset. The rainfall should 
diminish Tue morning from west to east. Low temps will be 
muggier in the mid 50s to lower 60s.

KEY MESSAGE 2...SPC has maintained a Marginal Risk (Level 1 of
5) for severe t-storms for locations south and west of the 
Greater Capital Region/Berkshires. The areas highlighted are 
the eastern Catskills, mid Hudson Valley, southern Taconics and
NW CT as well as the western Mohawk Valley of southern Herkimer
County. It is a tricky forecast to see where the warm 
front/boundary sets-up, as some of the guidance like the GFS/NAM
show the boundary stalling south of the Capital Region with the
front acting like a backdoor cold front, as sfc ridging builds 
back in from southeast Quebec and northern New England. The 
forecast area could be caught in clouds most of the day with 
north/northeast winds especially from the I-90 corridor north. 
However, the latest HREF guidance does show the best 0-6 km deep
shear of 40-45 KT with mean SBCAPEs of 1000-1500 J/kg overlay 
for the south/southwest zones in the Marginal Risk. Mid level 
lapse rates look decent towards I-84. Some deep organized 
convection could form with some diurnal heating on the warm side
of the boundary or outflow boundaries with strong to severe 
thunderstorms with damaging winds and large hail, as well as 
locally heavy rainfall due to the above normal PWATS. The severe
threat looks to be in the mid afternoon into early evening. We 
kept PoPs in the chance to low likely range (35-60%) prior to 
midnight. 

Another ridge roller disturbance looks to arrive for Wed with a
more robust heavy rain/flash flood threat and additional strong
to severe thunderstorms. Nonetheless, WPC maintains a Marginal
Risk in the Day 2 ERO for Tue-Tue night across the forecast 
area. Max temps were lowered some on Tue below the NBM with the 
clouds and back door front likely south of Albany. We leaned 
closer to an NBM/MAVMOS blend. We did not go as cool as the 
METMOS values. Highs in the mid 60s to mid 70s will be common 
from the Capital Region north and 70s to around 80F south. 

KEY MESSAGE  3...A strong short-wave in the west/northwest flow
around the rim of the ridge arrives for WED. The frontal 
boundary attempts to lift back to north/northeast across the 
region. The 0-6 km shear is strong, but the instability looks 
elevated initially. However, if we break into a warm sector some
strong to severe convection could form with the MCS/wave with 
moderate to large instability. The threat for strong storms 
looks like it would be greatest from the Capital Region 
southward. SPC with the latest Day 3 has most of the region in 
general thunder with a Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 5) just grazing
Ulster County for an isolated severe threat. 

Strong theta-e advection occurs with the wave with PWATs

back building could yield some isolated to scattered instances 
of flash flooding. WPC has locations mainly south/southwest of
